stem.text: Using a gel buffered at pH 7.6, electrophoresis is performed on a mixture of three amino acids: asparagine, histidine and lysine.

stem.caption: Figure 9.1
stem.alt: A horizontal electrophoresis strip with the positive electrode on the left and the negative electrode on the right; an x in the middle marks where the mixture is applied.

stem.text: The isoelectric points of these amino acids are given in Table 9.1.
Describe the direction of movement of each amino acid during the electrophoresis.

guidance: A ecf for bullets 2 and 6 if charges and directions are reversed.
A bullets 2, 4 and 6 from diagram only if directions not mentioned.

points.text: asparagine moves left / towards the positive/anode
histidine is a zwitterion / neutral / uncharged
lysine moves right / towards the negative/cathode

markScheme.note: Under the bullets the MS reprints the electrophoresis strip of Figure 9.1 (+ on the left, – on the right, x where the mixture is applied) to fix ‘left’ and ‘right’; it is not reproduced here.

explanation.text: At its isoelectric point an amino acid exists as a zwitterion with no overall charge. In a buffer with pH above its isoelectric point it loses H<sup>+</sup> and becomes negative; below its isoelectric point it gains H<sup>+</sup> and becomes positive.

At pH 7.6: asparagine (pI 5.4) is negative and moves left towards the + electrode (anode). Histidine (pI 7.6) is at its isoelectric point, uncharged, and stays at x. Lysine (pI 9.7) is positive and moves right towards the – electrode (cathode).
Each pair of points (charge and direction for one amino acid) is worth one mark.

reasoningChain: Compare buffer pH (7.6) with each pI.
pH > pI: negative, moves to +. pH = pI: neutral, stays. pH < pI: positive, moves to –.
Asparagine to the left (+), histidine stays, lysine to the right (–).

inferredMistakes.text: Reversing the rule, e.g. saying asparagine is positive because its pI is lower than the pH.
Saying histidine moves slowly rather than not at all.
Giving directions without explaining the charge on each amino acid.

stem.text: Serine, H<sub>2</sub>NCH(CH<sub>2</sub>OH)COOH, is an amino acid. It exists as a pair of optical isomers.
Draw diagrams in Figure 9.2 to show the three-dimensional structures of the two optical isomers of serine.

stem.caption: Figure 9.2
stem.alt: Two empty boxes for drawing the two optical isomers of serine.

guidance: No connectivity penalty for any group
may see RH structure same orientation as LH structure with any 2 groups switched.

points.text: two 3D mirror-image structures of serine (see figure)

figure.alt: From the MS: two mirror-image 3D structures of serine either side of a dashed mirror line. Left: COOH at the top, HOCH2 on a hashed bond, H on a plain bond, NH2 on a wedge. Right: COOH at the top, H on a plain bond, CH2OH on a hashed bond, NH2 on a wedge.

explanation.text: The chiral centre is the central carbon, bonded to four different groups: H, NH<sub>2</sub>, COOH and CH<sub>2</sub>OH. Draw it as a tetrahedron (two bonds in the plane, one wedge, one hashed) and draw the second isomer as its mirror image.

Swapping any two groups on one drawing also gives the other enantiomer, so the second structure need not be a reflection, as long as it is a different isomer. All three requirements (3D, correct formulae, different isomers) are needed for the one mark.

reasoningChain: Find the chiral C: H, NH<sub>2</sub>, COOH, CH<sub>2</sub>OH.
Draw one isomer with tetrahedral 3D bonds.
Draw its mirror image (or swap two groups).

inferredMistakes.text: Drawing two flat structures without wedge and hashed bonds.
Drawing the same isomer twice, e.g. rotating it instead of reflecting it.
Making a formula error, such as CH<sub>2</sub>OH written as CH<sub>3</sub>OH or a missing H.

stem.text: Give the name for a mixture containing equal amounts of the two optical isomers.

explanation.text: An equimolar mixture of two enantiomers is a racemic mixture (racemate). It is optically inactive overall because the rotations of the two isomers cancel.

reasoningChain: Equal amounts of both enantiomers: racemic mixture.

inferredMistakes.text: Writing ‘optically inactive mixture’ or ‘enantiomers’, which describe a property or the components, not the name of the mixture.

stem.text: Describe two properties that are different for the two optical isomers.

guidance: A biological reactivity / biochemistry. / biological effects / bioactivity.

points.text: M1 effect on/rotation of plane polarised light

explanation.text: Enantiomers have identical physical and chemical properties except two: they rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions (by the same angle), and they can have different biological activity because enzymes and receptors are chiral and fit only one isomer.
‘Angle of rotation’ is ignored because the angle is the same; it is the direction that differs. ‘Optical activity’ is ignored because both isomers are optically active.

reasoningChain: Property 1: effect on (direction of rotation of) plane-polarised light.
Property 2: biological activity / interaction with enzymes.

inferredMistakes.text: Saying the isomers rotate light by different angles; they rotate it by equal angles in opposite directions.
Giving a physical property such as melting point or solubility, which is the same for both enantiomers.
Describing the structures (mirror images) instead of a property; the MS ignores this.

stem.text: Serine is treated with an excess of phosphorus pentachloride, PCl5.
The phosphorus-containing product of this reaction is POCl3.
Complete the equation for this reaction. Use the structural formula of the organic product.

guidance: A [1] if molecular formula used, C3H5NOCl2 as only mistake.
A [1] if only one OH substituted and otherwise all correct.
after:
A ammonium salt but beware balancing with HCl, e.g.
H2NCH(CH2OH)COOH + 2PCl5 → 2POCl3 + HCl + ClH3NCH(CH2Cl)COCl

explanation.text: PCl<sub>5</sub> replaces every –OH with –Cl and gives POCl<sub>3</sub> + HCl each time. Serine has two OH groups: the alcohol –CH<sub>2</sub>OH becomes –CH<sub>2</sub>Cl, and the carboxylic acid –COOH becomes the acyl chloride –COCl. So two PCl<sub>5</sub> are needed.

The full equation is H<sub>2</sub>NCH(CH<sub>2</sub>OH)COOH + 2PCl<sub>5</sub> → 2POCl<sub>3</sub> + 2HCl + H<sub>2</sub>NCH(CH<sub>2</sub>Cl)COCl. The ammonium salt is also accepted if HCl is balanced: one HCl is used to protonate the NH<sub>2</sub>.

reasoningChain: Count OH groups in serine: two (CH<sub>2</sub>OH and COOH).
Each OH + PCl<sub>5</sub> → Cl + POCl<sub>3</sub> + HCl.

inferredMistakes.text: Substituting only the COOH group, leaving CH<sub>2</sub>OH unchanged.
Replacing the NH<sub>2</sub> group with Cl as well; PCl<sub>5</sub> does not react with amines this way.
Using 1 PCl<sub>5</sub>, or forgetting HCl, so the equation does not balance.

issues.note: MS 答案栏底部重印了 Figure 9.1 的电泳条（+ 左、– 右），只是为了说明 left/right，与 QP 图相同，未截图，写在 markScheme.note 里。
答案栏第一行是完整方程式，放在 markScheme.instruction；M1/M2 是 points；答案栏末尾 'A ammonium salt but beware balancing with HCl, e.g. …' 放在 markScheme.after。
'No connectivity penalty for any group' 和 'may see RH structure same orientation as LH structure with any 2 groups switched.' 原文没有标点隔开，按两条 guidance 转录。答案只有图，没有文字，points 写简短描述。
跨章题：(a) 是 34.4 氨基酸电泳，(b) 主要是 29.4 光学异构 + 33.1/16.1 PCl5 反应。以氨基酸为主线，放在第 34 章 Nitrogen compounds 的 Cross-topic。
